text.p: These are the leading stories in the Turkish press on Monday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
SABAH

- Islamist Prime Minister Necmettin Erbakan is pressurising his conservative coalition partners, the True Path Party (DYP) to vote on a draft law that would save Erbakan's party from a court case threatening it with closure.
- The Islamist-led government planned to sign a mid-term stability programme with International Monetary Fund (IMF), but gave up on the idea when deciding to hold early elections.
MILLIYET
- The Islamist-led government continues to hold back an extra subdisy to the armed forces which was to help pay for their cross-border operation in northern Iraq.
HURRIYET
- Turkey's military top brass will brief reporters and state prosecutors on Tuesday about the Islamist invesment and education.
- Automotive output rose by 14.7 percent in May 1997 compared to the same period last year.
YENI YUZYIL
- The Islamist-led government has shelved a military-sponsored plan to extend compulsory education to eight years now that early elections are on the agenda.
RADIKAL
- Erbakan said the date for the early election would be October 19.
DUNYA
- Russia is taking measures to tax the unregistered suitcase trading with Turkey.
- The disagreement between the Privatisation Board and the energy ministry rocked the evaluation of tenders for five power plants.
ZAMAN
- Statements by Erbakan and the military have lead to confusion over when to put an end to the cross-border operation into nothern Iraq.
CUMHURIYET
- Erbakan slipped up at a party meeting saying the operation in northern Iraq was coming to an end, but was forced to correct himself later after the news caused shock in military circles.
- Turkish businessmen prefer to dress in Turkish-made suits.
